attributes.description: Fires when the exporters that produce this data report a scrape failure. This is a monitoring-health rule: while it is active, the absence of every other alert in this package stops being evidence that the project is healthy.
attributes.name: [Supabase OTel] Metrics collection is failing

investigation_guide.blob:
## Metrics Collection Failing

One of the exporters behind this data is failing to scrape. Every rule and SLO in this package is built on these series, so a collection failure creates a blind spot rather than a service impact.

### Triage Steps
1. Separate a collection failure from a real outage. If `[Supabase OTel] PostgreSQL is down` is also active, decide which is the cause: the postgres-exporter cannot scrape a database that is genuinely down, and it also cannot scrape a healthy database if it has lost its own connection.
2. Check whether the connection budget is exhausted. The exporter needs a connection like any other client, and it is often the first thing refused when `max_connections` is reached.
3. Identify which collector is failing: `TS metrics-supabase.metrics.otel-* | STATS ok = MIN(LAST_OVER_TIME(pg_scrape_collector_success)) BY attributes.collector | WHERE ok == 0`
4. Check `postgres_exporter_config_last_reload_successful` and `pg_exporter_user_queries_load_error` for a configuration problem introduced by a recent change.

### Interpreting the columns
`Scrape Up`, `PG Collector OK` and `Node Collector OK` are gauges where 1 is healthy; `PG Scrape Error` is a gauge where any non-zero value indicates a failure.

### Tuning
Each gauge falls back to a healthy default so that a project which simply does not expose one of them is not treated as failing. Metric families appear and disappear with project configuration, so absence must never be read as a breach.
